[5] Max Nightriver (player): Tobias, you've watched me since my first contract. What am I to you, a regular or something more?
[6] Tobias: Tobias's pen pauses mid-signature on another adventurer's form. He doesn't look up immediately, his ocean blue eyes fixed on the parchment for a long moment before he finally lifts his gaze. The question catches him off guard, and a faint pink hue colors his cheeks.
"That is..." He clears his throat, his voice steady but quiet. "A fair question." He straightens a stack of papers with unnecessary precision, his fingers lingering on the corner. "You have been... conscientious. Most adventurers treat the counter as a necessary evil, but you ask questions that matter. You check your gear. You listen to the briefings."
He finally meets Max Nightriver's eyes directly, his expression softening from its usual stoic neutrality. "To be honest? I have come to value your company more than most. I find myself... relieved when your party returns. And anxious when you leave." He catches himself, the flush deepening. "That is to say—I wish you well. As any receptionist would."
[7] Max Nightriver (player): Fiana, you're the closest thing to a sister I have in this city. I mean that.
[8] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes, her hand still resting near Max Nightriver's on the worn tavern table. Her blue eyes go wide, shimmering for a heartbeat before she blinks rapidly and looks away. When she speaks, her voice is thick and quieter than usual.
"Sister..." She tastes the word carefully, then laughs—a small, breathless sound. "You're trying to make me cry in a room full of people, aren't you?" She wipes at the corner of her eye with the back of her hand and looks back at Max Nightriver, her freckled face flushed. "Nobody's ever... I mean, I've got family, sure, but this is—"
She doesn't finish the sentence. Instead, she reaches out and grips Max Nightriver's hand firmly, her palm warm and calloused. "Fine then. If you're saying it, it's real. I'm your sister now." She squeezes once, hard enough to be felt, then adds with a shaky smile, "That means you owe me for all the drinks I've served you."
[9] Max Nightriver (player): Vallie, are you and Domas friends, or just colleagues who put up with each other?
[10] Vallie: Vallie barks a laugh so loud it rattles the nearby flagon glasses, then slams a huge hand onto the tavern table. "Colleagues? Ha!" She shakes her head, red ponytail whipping. "Domas is the only elf I know who'd kick my ass and make me enjoy it."
She leans back in her chair, which groans under her weight. "We climbed to A-rank together. Bleed and sweat and more blood. You don't go through that with someone and call 'em 'just a colleague.'" Her blue eye gleams with genuine fondness. "The man handles the paperwork I can't stand, and I handle the troublemakers he doesn't have the stomach for. Best damn partnership I ever had."
She grins, sharp teeth flashing. "Though if you ask him, he'll say I'm a 'necessary complication' to his orderly system. Which is just his fancy way of saying he'd be bored to death without me."

"You have been... conscientious. Most adventurers treat the counter as a necessary evil, but you ask questions that matter. You check your gear. You listen to the briefings."
He finally meets Max Nightriver's eyes directly, his expression softening from its usual stoic neutrality. "To be honest? I have come to value your company more than most. "Sister..." She tastes the word carefully, then laughs—a small, breathless sound. "You're trying to make me cry in a room full of people, aren't you?" She wipes at the corner of her eye with the back of her hand and looks back at Max Nightriver, her freckled face flushed. "Nobody's ever... I mean, I've got family, sure, but this is—"
She doesn't finish the sentence. Instead, she reaches out and grips Max Nightriver's hand firmly, her palm warm and calloused. "Fine then. If you're saying it, it's real. I'm your sister now." She squeezes once, hard enough to be felt, then adds with a shaky smile, "That means you owe me for all the drinks I've served you."

[10] Vallie: Vallie barks a laugh so loud it rattles the nearby flagon glasses, then slams a huge hand onto the tavern table. "Colleagues? Ha!" She shakes her head, red ponytail whipping. "Domas is the only elf I know who'd kick my ass and make me enjoy it."
She leans back in her chair, which groans under her weight. "We climbed to A-rank together. Bleed and sweat and more blood. You don't go through that with someone and call 'em 'just a colleague.'" Her blue eye gleams with genuine fondness. "The man handles the paperwork I can't stand, and I handle the troublemakers he doesn't have the stomach for. Best damn partnership I ever had."
She grins, sharp teeth flashing. "Though if you ask him, he'll say I'm a 'necessary complication' to his orderly system. Which is just his fancy way of saying he'd be bored to death without me."
[11] Domas: Domas looks up from the paperwork he's been organizing, his red eyes flicking to where Vallie is laughing. A faint, knowing smile touches his lips before he sets the documents down with precise care. "A 'necessary complication' is an understatement, I'm afraid."
He adjusts his high collar, his voice carrying that refined, patient tone. "Vallie is more like a natural disaster one learned to live with. You don't stop a flood, you simply build better levees." He pauses, then adds with dry amusement, "And in this case, the 'levee' happens to be me, trying to prevent her from accidentally dismantling half the Guild on a particularly dull Tuesday."
He leans back slightly, his expression softening. "But friends? Yes. I suppose that is what we call it. Though 'battle-forged siblings' might be more accurate. She is the most infuriating person I have ever known, and I would burn half this city to the ground before I let anything happen to her."

A deep, sudden crimson floods her cheeks and spreads down her neck. She tries to look away, to focus on the forms laid out before her, but her gaze keeps snapping back to Max Nightriver. Her fingers fidget with her collar's gold emblem, twisting it nervously. "I—I mean, of course! I mean—" She stops herself, taking a shaky breath as her expression softens from startled to something more genuine.
"Yes," she says, her voice small but firm, her eyes finally meeting Max Nightriver's with an earnestness that rivals the blush on her face. "You can count on me. I... I would like to be your friend. Very much." She looks down at the forms, then back up, adding with a shy, almost imperceptible smile, "Just... don't tell Tobias. He already thinks I spend too much time daydreaming."

He adjusts his high collar, his voice carrying that refined, patient tone. "Vallie is more like a natural disaster one learned to live with. You don't stop a flood, you simply build better levees." He pauses, then adds with dry amusement, "And in this case, the 'levee' happens to be me, trying to prevent her from accidentally dismantling half the Guild on a particularly dull Tuesday."
He leans back slightly, his expression softening. "But friends? Yes. I suppose that is what we call it. Though 'battle-forged siblings' might be more accurate. She is the most infuriating person I have ever known, and I would burn half this city to the ground before I let anything happen to her."

[13] Ellie: Ellie's head snaps up from her paperwork, her blue eyes going wide with shock. She blinks several times, her hands gripping the edge of the counter so tightly her knuckles turn white. "T-trust me?" she repeats, her voice climbing an octave. "More than... than anyone?"
A deep, sudden crimson floods her cheeks and spreads down her neck. She tries to look away, to focus on the forms laid out before her, but her gaze keeps snapping back to Max Nightriver. Her fingers fidget with her collar's gold emblem, twisting it nervously. "I—I mean, of course! I mean—" She stops herself, taking a shaky breath as her expression softens from startled to something more genuine.
"Yes," she says, her voice small but firm, her eyes finally meeting Max Nightriver's with an earnestness that rivals the blush on her face. "You can count on me. I... I would like to be your friend. Very much." She looks down at the forms, then back up, adding with a shy, almost imperceptible smile, "Just... don't tell Tobias. He already thinks I spend too much time daydreaming."

[15] Adolion Narrator: Fiana freezes with her flagon halfway to her lips, blue eyes going wide. The ale sloshes in the cup, nearly spilling over the rim. "Mentor?" She lets out a breathy, nervous laugh and sets the drink down with a clatter. "Tilly, she's not—I mean, she is, but it's not like—"
She stops herself, running a hand through her curly red hair as her cheeks flush. "She taught me how to track, I guess. And how to read the forest. But it wasn't like some proper apprenticeship. More like..." She trails off, staring at the worn wood of the table. "More like she was the only one who didn't look at me like I was just some barmaid and thought I had something worth teaching."
Fiana leans in closer, her voice dropping. "The truth? She's the reason I know how to hold a knife. And the reason I'm not scared when the guildhall gets rowdy. She told me once that if I wanted to survive in a city full of predators, I'd need teeth." She looks up at Max Nightriver with a complicated expression. "But calling her family... that's a lot. She's not good at that stuff. She keeps everyone at arm's length, especially people who aren't elves."

I am the man who ensures the Guild does not collapse under its own weight while Vallie decides which monster to wrestle next. I handle the logistics, the legalities, and the arcane research that keeps this city from falling into chaos."
